instagram_caption:
What if the Sun vanished at 2:00 pm on a summer afternoon at Bondi? ☀️

Nobody would notice. Sunlight takes about 8 minutes 20 seconds to cross the 149.6 million km to Earth, so the last of it would still be on its way. Changes in gravity travel at the speed of light too, so Earth would keep circling the empty spot for those same 8 minutes 20 seconds.

Then the sky goes black. About 1.3 seconds later the Moon goes out as well: moonlight is just sunlight bounced back to us, and the Moon is 1.3 light-seconds away.

After that, Earth flies off in a straight line at about 107,000 km/h, the speed it was orbiting at. Scientists estimate the average surface would fall below −18 °C within about a week, and to around −73 °C within a year.

This is fiction. But the sunlight on your skin right now really did leave the Sun about 8 minutes 20 seconds ago.

Did you spot him? 👀
